A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched reliably despite relocation and the added Appendix A.2.

before.justification: V2 reports original kernel simulations, synthetic regression experiments, and classification results on MNIST, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, including the experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds a matched-training-loss comparison on MNIST in Appendix A.2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The residual scaling rule, network construction, training objective and early-stopping approach are retained. V3 explicitly names the mirrored-network initialization in Section 2.1, but this construction was already documented in v2 Appendix B.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic spherical data, MNIST, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet. The new matched-loss experiment uses the retained MNIST classification task. Appendix A's new references to reasoning, tool use and embodied intelligence do not represent additional evaluations.

E2.justification: V3 substantially broadens practical method comparisons by adding Fixup, ReZero and a DeepNorm-style scaling variant alongside Base and Proposed in Table 1. V2 compared scaling exponents and unscaled/normalization controls without evaluating these named alternatives. The DeepNorm comparator uses only its scaling rule, not the complete method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a protocol measuring test accuracy when training loss reaches approximately 0.05, plus minimum training loss within equal epoch budgets. This focused control supplements the existing evaluations; the stated settings of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new matched-loss analysis tests whether scaling's generalization advantage persists at comparable optimization levels, extending v2's argument based on similar training accuracy. Existing scaling/depth sweeps and kernel-behavior analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains standard-error reporting over trials. The new Table 1 provides point estimates without introducing run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure is revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds matched-loss MNIST accuracies of 96.66%, 97.84%, 97.49%, 97.30% and 97.29% for Base, Fixup, ReZero, DeepNorm and Proposed, respectively, plus best-training-loss results. These are new results under the added protocol; the results plotted in Figures 1–6 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.2 changes the kernel defining the source-condition RKHS from r to the one-hidden-layer RNTK r^(1). This refines the formal hypothesis to align with the existing limiting-kernel argument in Appendix E.1. The theorem bounds and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: uniform ResNet–RNTK generalization correspondence, asymptotic unlearnability with constant scaling, and minimax rates with rapidly decaying scaling and early stopping. The additional experiment supports these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V3 acknowledges that saturated training accuracy can conceal different training losses and interprets Table 1 as mechanistic support despite the proposed rule trailing stronger baselines. Section 5 and Appendix A also explicitly limit empirical applicability to relatively modest models and image-classification datasets.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly documents that the DeepNorm comparator adopts only its residual scaling rule, excluding additional design choices such as dedicated initialization. Existing implementation disclosures are retained; the new experiment's architecture and numerical training budget are not specified.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 substantially expands positioning through signal-propagation and edge-of-chaos literature, including Poole, Schoenholz, Yang and Fischer, and sharper comparisons with earlier RNTK analyses. V3 also adds the finite-depth ResNet work of Lai et al. (2023b), broad application references in Appendix A, and replaces the cited Arora et al. (2019) paper with a different work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the introduction, related work, architecture and training exposition. Further Discussion becomes Section 3.3, the existing Appendix A becomes A.1 alongside new A.2, and acknowledgements are added. The principal narrative order and most existing exposition are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 1 and rearranges Appendix A, placing Figure 6 beside the table instead of wrapping the Transformer discussion around it. Existing figures retain their graphical content, with some placement changes; the main document and proof layouts remain broadly consistent.

improvement.justification: The matched-loss MNIST comparison addresses a concrete weakness in v2's use of similar training accuracy to distinguish optimization from generalization. Clearer research positioning, the refined source condition and explicit empirical limitations also improve precision. The gain remains limited: the main theory and previous results are retained, and the new comparison lacks full implementation and uncertainty details.
